clue.text: With an effort, in one continuous period

definitions.meaning: done only by straining, a push beyond what is comfortable
done without a break, all in one go

explanation.surface: Someone describes a hard, unbroken spell of work.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom covers both managing something only by straining, and doing it without interruption, such as working ten hours in a single go.

clue.text: Patient learnt to suffer treatment

indicators.note: the letters undergo treatment, being worked over and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A hospital patient learnt to put up with medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like the noun from the surface's hospital; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forbearing puts up with things calmly; the adjective sense of patient.

clue.text: No introduction needed for upcoming Murdoch title

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the introduction of a word is its opening letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: Iris Murdoch was the Anglo-Irish novelist and philosopher

explanation.surface: Rupert Murdoch's knighthood is on its way, and he needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the press baron Rupert Murdoch; it is the novelist Iris Murdoch. Dropping her first letter leaves RIS, which 'upcoming' turns upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The honorific used before a knight's name, like Dame for a woman, is a title.

clue.text: Took exam again (scripture test)

parts.note: RE, religious education, is the school subject once called scripture
SAT is a standardised test, as in American college entrance or English school SATs

explanation.surface: A student retook an exam, this time a scripture test.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit an exam a second time is to retake it; the past tense matches 'took'.

clue.text: Some skin lotions are currently under discussion

definitions.meaning: lotions applied to the surface of the body rather than swallowed are described in medicine this way
of current interest, in the news now

explanation.surface: Some skin lotions are being talked about at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a sentence missing its last word: a lotion applied externally is described with this medical term.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine the word means applied to the body's surface; in general use it means dealing with current events.

clue.text: Weapon husband's given with a brusque flourish

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for husband, as in family trees

indicators.note: a flourish is an ornamental twirl, so the following letters are waved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A husband is handed a weapon with a curt, showy gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: An early portable matchlock gun used from the 15th to the 17th century.

clue.text: Catch one's breath when getting checked by doctor

indicators.note: being checked, held in, by something means sitting inside it

parts.note: GP, a general practitioner, is a family doctor
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A patient becomes breathless while a doctor examines them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sharp intake of air, as when surprised or exhausted.

clue.text: Fail to act like most tourists in china?

definitions.meaning: said of a business that collapses or is ruined

definitions.text: act like most tourists in china?
definitions.meaning: visitors to China nearly all head for its Great Wall; the lower-case china hides the country

explanation.surface: A traveller fails to behave like most visitors to China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fail to act' looks like one phrase; the break comes after 'Fail'. The lower-case 'china' disguises the country, whose Great Wall most tourists visit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be ruined, as a business is, and literally describes visiting China's Great Wall, which almost every tourist there does.

clue.text: Take a shine to a girl

indicators.note: to here means added to, so one piece is put next to the other

parts.note: sheen means a shine or lustre

explanation.surface: Someone takes a liking to a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take a shine to' is the idiom for growing fond of; here 'shine' simply gives SHEEN and 'Take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's forename, a Scottish form of Jane.

clue.text: In bother, addict turns and gets angry

indicators.note: In tells us one piece goes inside the word for bother

parts.note: a flap is a state of fluster or bother

indicators.note: turns signals that the word for addict is read backwards

parts.note: a user is a drug addict

explanation.surface: In a state, a drug addict turns nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bother' looks like part of the surface's fluster, but FLAP is the container cut open by the turned addict.
explanation.definitionFit: To erupt in sudden temper, like a fire suddenly blazing.

clue.text: Dog more likely to snarl without one?

indicators.note: without signals that the letter for one is taken out

parts.note: rattier is the comparative of ratty, British slang for irritable and snappish
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Would a dog be more inclined to growl if it were missing one?
explanation.walkthrough: RATTY is British slang for bad-tempered; its comparative loses its I.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier or similar breed kept to catch rodents.

clue.text: It may be associated with expert financier, principally

definitions.text: It may be associated with expert financier, principally

indicators.note: associated with means joined to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a pro is an expert, a professional

indicators.note: principally means first or chiefly, so only the opening letter of financier is used

explanation.surface: Gain is what a skilled money man is mainly linked with.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: PRO, F and IT, joined, name what an expert financier chiefly brings.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial gain is what a skilful money manager is chiefly known for making.

clue.text: Unsuccessful enterprise lands roofer in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder, so they are mixed up

explanation.surface: A failed venture lands a roofer in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointless task with no hope of success, a fruitless mission.

clue.text: Maths activity of some importance

definitions.meaning: reckoning numbers one by one, an early arithmetic skill
carrying weight, mattering, as a vote does

explanation.surface: Arithmetic is an important activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbering things in sequence is basic arithmetic, and something that matters can be said to carry weight.

clue.text: Very upset since balloon burst

indicators.note: a burst balloon scatters, so these letters are blown apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A child is distraught because the balloon has popped.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond comfort, unable to be cheered: extremely distressed.

clue.text: Jewish reformed synagogue's opening — I'd preach

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
reformed means formed again, so the letters are rearranged; it also plays on Reform Judaism

explanation.surface: A preacher speaks at the opening of a Reform synagogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' rearranges I'D PREACH into EPHARDIC, set after S, the opening of 'synagogue's'; it also nods to Reform Judaism.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes Jews of Spanish and Portuguese descent and their traditions.

clue.text: Conventional support to listener is a barrier

parts.note: stock means standard or conventional, as in a stock response

indicators.note: to a listener means as heard, so the word for support is taken by its sound

parts.note: aid means help or support

explanation.surface: Traditional backing for an audience turns out to be an obstacle.
explanation.walkthrough: AID, heard, is spelt ADE, as in lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure or defensive wall made of upright wooden posts.

clue.text: Drugs and drink put squeeze on workers

parts.note: sup means to drink, to sip
press means squeeze
worker ants: workers is a common crossword clue for ants or bees

explanation.surface: Booze and pills are used to pressure employees.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicines that hold back a bodily function, such as appetite or coughing.

clue.text: Holding a fine one, a sailor's up for liqueur

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one group of letters sits inside the other
in a down clue, up means the words for a sailor are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, as in Jack Tar
F stands for fine, as in pencil and quality grading
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Holding a good one, a sailor gets up to order a liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns A TAR into RATA; 'Holding' puts AFI inside it, before the last A.
explanation.definitionFit: A liqueur flavoured with almonds or fruit kernels; also a biscuit of that flavour.

clue.text: Draw lots shortly after start of discussion

indicators.note: after places the trimmed word for lots behind the first letter
the start of a word is its first letter
shortly means cut short, so the word for lots loses its last letter

parts.note: oodles means lots, a large amount

explanation.surface: Lots are drawn soon after a discussion begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To scribble idly, making aimless sketches.

clue.text: Right, work is over: put oven on for the meat

indicators.note: over signals that the preceding pair of words turns back to front

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
an oast is a kiln for drying hops, a kind of oven

explanation.surface: Work done, the cook puts the oven on for the joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is over' turns RT and OP into POTR; 'put ... on' adds OAST, a hop-drying kiln common in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint of beef braised slowly in a lidded dish.

clue.text: Ill will foreign country's shown to Anglican church

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church

explanation.surface: A foreign country shows hostility to the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite, the desire to harm others.

clue.text: Targets a philosopher when speaking

indicators.note: when spoken out loud the philosopher's name gives the letters we want

parts.note: Karl Marx was the German philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher sets out his aims in a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Objects aimed at, such as a swindler's victims or a shooter's bullseyes.

clue.text: Lear in part had raw deal, suffering setback

indicators.note: a setback is a turning back, so the letters run in reverse
in part means only a portion of these words is used

explanation.surface: King Lear was partly hard done by, and suffered a reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear' suggests Shakespeare's king, but it is the Victorian nonsense poet; 'in part' takes DRAWDE from 'had raw deal' and 'suffering setback' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian nonsense poet Lear bore this forename.

clue.text: Display of enthusiasm by old friend for a gemstone

parts.note: fire means passion or ardour shown openly
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: An old friend shows passion over a precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A precious stone with flame-coloured flashes, mined in Mexico.

clue.text: Lout with ball upset soccer players

parts.note: O resembles a ball in shape

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read upward

parts.note: FA, the Football Association, runs English soccer

explanation.surface: A yob with a football upsets the team.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy, boorish person; a yob.

clue.text: Very dull

definitions.meaning: an intensifier meaning absolutely or exactly, as in '... easy' or '... centre'
lacking life or sparkle, like a flat colour or a lifeless party

explanation.definitionFit: Used as an intensifier meaning absolutely, and also meaning lifeless or flat.

clue.text: Ordered to be kept secret

definitions.meaning: arranged in classes or categories, sorted
officially restricted from public knowledge, like government documents

explanation.surface: A government document is ordered to be kept confidential.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorted into categories, and officially restricted, as sensitive government papers are.
